summary: King County L-4 cab site 8 miles south of Snoqualmie Pass; cab built 1935, gone by 1972 (sources differ on removed or destroyed); now a hike.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a rock talus outcrop at the most southern point of the summit
facts.status_note: The cab came down in 1972; the summit site and some anchor lines remain

access.note: Reached on foot by a steep, rocky road and an abandoned trail; the Mountaineers describe it as a hike

visit.trail_note: High clearance gets closest to the start; the walk runs from 1/2 mile to 2 miles depending on where you park

events.note: Panoramic photographs dated 1934 taken from the summit; they appear to show a lookout camp
L-4 cab on the south point of the rock talus outcrop
USGS placed a monument at the lookout site
Register says removed; Firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.quote: This L-4 cab was built in 1935 and removed in 1972.
Meadow Mountain Lookout panoramic 8-10-1934 (N) - courtesy of National Archives-Pacific Northwest Region

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
eight miles south of Snoqualmie Pass

evidence.quote: In 1934, panoramic photos were taken from the summit with what appears to be a lookout camp.
The next year, a structure was built in 1935, it was an L-4 cab that remained until 1972.

evidence.supports: site on the most southern point of a rock talus outcrop
evidence.quote: The lookout was located at the most southern point on a prominent rock talus outcrop that can't grow trees
In 1958, the USGS placed a monument at the lookout site

evidence.quote: Distance: 1/2 mile up to 2 miles, depending on where you park

evidence.quote: Hike to an abandoned, seldom visited, fire lookout site south of Snoqualmie Pass.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1972; Firelookout.com says destroyed. Both date it to 1972. The sources do not say who took it down.

notes_for_editor: Record checked: coordinates match the FFLOS page (47.29997, -121.44813), and county, agency and elevation (1,650 m) match. Sources agree on 1935 and 1972 but disagree on removed vs destroyed. No staffing or fire information in the four sources. Access level 'public' rests on the Mountaineers hike description; no closure notice was checked. Not checked on the ground.
